finding: The headline leg of TEST-20 ('no horizontal overflow at 390/768/1280px') can never fail. The builder renders inside SettingsPage.tsx:331 `<div className="flex-1 overflow-hidden">` and inside SettingsPageContainer's DivScrollY (OverlayScrollbars scroll host), so no builder child can ever propagate width to the document: `document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth - clientWidth` is structurally 0 whatever the builder renders. A step list, header row, name Input or tool card 900px wide at a 390px viewport would be CLIPPED (invisible, unreachable) and this assertion still returns 0 <= 1. Only the finding boxes (line 160-167) and the four generated fields (line 194-196) are actually geometry-checked; every other element on the page is unverified. ITEM-10 ('the owner reported it doesn't fit') is therefore not proven by the assertion that names it.

TEST-1 is the [acceptance] proof of INV-1 ('no raw schema/YAML key language ever reaches the person building a workflow'), but it only asserts that every registered code is a KEY of HUMAN_COPY (line 2626-2640). Key PRESENCE is not human language: an entry such as `"WORKFLOW_X": ({message}) => message`, or copy that names a wire field without a trailing colon ('This step's for_each must be a list', 'output_format must be json or text'), violates INV-1 and leaves this test GREEN. The complement lives in a NON-acceptance unit test (validationCopy.test.ts:72-95) whose screen is only a trailing-colon regex plus a four-token denylist (prompt_file|$defs|serde|snake_case), which those examples pass. So for a real, cheap-to-hit violation shape of INV-1, the invariant's designated acceptance test does not go RED.

Phantom leg. TESTS.md claims TEST-3 asserts 'no builder step form binds a FREE-TEXT control to a field whose values the system can enumerate'. `offendingBindings` actually clears a field as soon as ANY picker in the SAME FILE binds it (line 87-89), and ToolStepForm.tsx binds `step.tool` to BOTH a Combobox (:318-322) and an Input (:336-339). The tool field is therefore permanently exempt: a regression that makes free text the DEFAULT path (e.g. inverting `usePicker` at ToolStepForm.tsx:169-170, or the catalog silently failing) leaves both controls in the source and this scanner stays green. What is actually asserted is the much narrower 'no field is bound ONLY to a text box', not the claimed class rule.

TEST-21 silently drops fixture findings it cannot pattern-match. The regex requires `code:` then `layer:` then `location:` in that exact order, so the gallery's third seeded error — WORKFLOW_SANDBOX_FLAVOR_REQUIRED at gallery.tsx:509-515, which deliberately carries NO `location` — is never extracted and therefore never compared against the live backend, neither for its code/layer nor for its verbatim message. The `>= 3` guard at line 243-246 is satisfied by the other three findings, so that entry could drift back to a fabricated code and pre-humanised prose (exactly the defect TEST-21 exists to catch) with the test green. Any future locationless fixture finding is equally invisible.

The ~400-line hand-written Rust lexer added for the drift guard has no self-test: nothing proves `scan_rust_source` would actually FIND a newly added `ValidationError::at("semantic", "NEW_CODE", …)` site, or that its comment/string/char-literal/`#[cfg(test)]` skipping is correct. The two directional set comparisons (line 2617-2631) make an under-scan of an EXISTING code fail loudly ('listed but no longer emitted'), which is the safe direction — but a NEW emit site the lexer fails to read is invisible to BOTH sets simultaneously (not emitted, not registered), so the sets still agree, no copy is demanded, and a code with no human copy ships green. Concrete desync vectors with zero coverage: `skip_char_literal_or_lifetime` (:2123) mis-advancing on `'\u{1f600}'`-shaped input, `#[cfg(all(test, …))]` not matching the literal `#[cfg(test)]` check (:2180), and `raw_string_prefix` on `br#"`. A fixture-string negative control (feed the scanner a synthetic source containing a known code and assert it is found; feed one with the code in a comment and assert it is NOT) would close this.

The commit-on-blur machinery has zero coverage. (a) `pendingNumberClear` (:184-232) exists because InputNumber emits `undefined` for both 'cleared' and 'partial number being typed' — the named bug is 'a negative number could never be typed over an existing one'. No test types into an InputNumber character-by-character or blurs it; TEST-6 uses `fill('25')`, a single-shot set that never produces the `undefined` transition. (b) The Textarea `onBlur` -> `coerceToDeclared` + `sameValue` path (:275-278): `coerceToDeclared` is unit-tested in isolation, but the `json`/`textarea` control is never RENDERED by any test — the e2e mock server (builder-tools-mock-server.ts:153-208) declares no object/array/long-string property, so the json/textarea/multiselect/switch-with-default control arms and their blur wiring are never exercised end to end. A regression in either blur handler is undetectable.

Sticky template mode (`templateMode` latch, :103-109) and its escape (`clear-ref` button, :138-152) are untested. TEST-6 asserts the clear-ref button is VISIBLE (builder-tool-picker.spec.ts:309-311, 328-331) but never CLICKS it, so DEC-5's promise 'the switch to template mode is reversible / never a trap' is unproven — `setTemplateMode(false); commit('')` has no test. Nor is the bug the latch was written for covered: backspacing the closing `}}` of an inserted reference must NOT flip the control back to the typed one. Both are the exact regressions the code comments describe.

The synthetic 'not offered by this server any more' option (:179-198) has zero coverage anywhere — no unit test, no e2e, no gallery-driven assertion (grep for the literal string returns only the component). It is the guard against a saved-but-renamed upstream tool rendering as an EMPTY Combobox while the definition still carries the value — a silent data-loss shape the required-field check explicitly cannot catch. Related and equally uncovered: the 'Try again' button + `retryCatalog` (:205-210, :295-307) — the store's `invalidate` is unit-tested (ToolCatalog.store.test.ts:308-330) but the button that calls it is never clicked.

The panel's new error Alert (`wf-builder-validation-error`, :115-124) and the save-toast humanisation (WorkflowBuilderPage.tsx:84-95) are never rendered by any test. `parseInstallError` / `humaniseInstallError` are thoroughly unit-tested (validationCopy.test.ts:285-366), but nothing proves the WIRING: that `store.error` reaches the Alert, that the green 'No blocking errors.' claim is really suppressed while the last check failed (the stale-green defect the comment names), or that the save toast actually shows the humanised sentence instead of the raw `[semantic/CODE] step: message`. INV-1 is claimed to be 'a property of the SURFACE, not of one code path' — the second surface is only proven at the pure-function layer.

The WARNING half of the attribution surface is only ever asserted ABSENT. `wf-builder-step-warned-*` appears once, as `toHaveCount(0)` (:122), and `wf-builder-warnings` appears in no spec at all — so the warning badge (StepList.tsx:126-138) and the warnings list branch (BuilderValidationPanel.tsx:151-158) are never rendered positively by any test. `indexFindingsByStep` counts warnings correctly at the unit layer (validationCopy.test.ts:245-277), but a rendering regression in either warning surface would go undetected, and the `toHaveCount(0)` at :122 has no positive control that the badge can appear at all.

The enum `raw` round-trip — the defect toolSchemaForm.test.ts:308-341 was written for (an integer enum committing `"2"` instead of `2`, and a stored `2` rendering unselected) — is never exercised through the live Select control. The mock server's only enum is a STRING enum (`mode: ['semantic','keyword','hybrid']`), for which `optionValueForKey`/`optionKeyForValue` are identity functions, so TEST-5's enum leg (builder-tool-picker.spec.ts:243-251) would pass identically against the old `String(v)` implementation. Declaring one non-string enum property in the mock would make the ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:236-249 wiring falsifiable.

'no mapped copy leaks wire vocabulary to the author' loops over `HUMANISED_CODES` (= `Object.keys(HUMAN_COPY)`) with no assertion that the collection is non-empty. If HUMAN_COPY were emptied, renamed, or its export changed shape during a refactor, the loop body never runs and `assert.deepEqual(offenders, [])` passes vacuously. The Rust guard asserts `!humanised.is_empty()` (validate.rs:2632) but that is a different suite; this file should carry its own floor (the sibling scanner at noFreeTextEntityRef.test.ts:94-98 does exactly that).

TESTS.md's TEST-1 line describes the mechanism inaccurately in two ways: it says the codes scanned are those in 'validate.rs + ref_check.rs' (the guard scans the whole server crate plus the desktop crate — validate.rs:1950-1957) and that validationCopy.ts is 'read via include_str!' (it is read at RUNTIME with fs::read_to_string, validate.rs:1935-1939, deliberately so it cannot be a stale compiled-in snapshot). Both drifts are in the safe direction (the code is stronger than the claim), but the claim ledger is the artifact the merge gate reads, so it should describe what runs.

Every tool-step spec depends on the freshly-seeded MCP server appearing in `McpServer.servers`, which ToolCatalog.store.ts:236-238 documents as a PAGINATED slice ('a server beyond the loaded page resolves to unknown-server'). E2E specs share one backend/database per run and each of these four specs plus builder-step-kinds and builder-responsive seeds another server, so once the accumulated server count exceeds the loaded page the Server picker option `wf-builder-tool-server-opt-<name>` stops existing and the tool catalog degrades to the fallback. The failure direction is RED, not a false pass, but it is order-dependent across specs sharing the run.

TEST-7 waits 30000ms for the unreachable-server Alert while seeding that same server with `timeout_seconds: 30` (:351). The assertion budget equals the server's own configured upstream timeout, so any path where the backend actually spends its full timeout (rather than failing fast on DNS for `.invalid`) races the expect. Give the alert a budget strictly larger than the seeded `timeout_seconds`.

`generatedField()` locates the label/description block by XPath `ancestor::div[contains(@class,"flex-col")][1]`, coupling TEST-5's acceptance assertions (requiredness `*`, description, 'Defaults to 10.') to LabeledControl's Tailwind class string. A purely cosmetic change to that wrapper's classes retargets the ancestor and breaks the acceptance proof of INV-4. The failure direction is red, so this is polish, not vacuity — but a `data-slot`/testid anchor on the LabeledControl root would decouple it.

REJECTED — considered coverage inflation (one spec file carrying four TEST-IDs). It is not: TEST-4/5/6/7 are four separate `test()` blocks with independent fixtures, independent mock lifecycles and disjoint assertions (option set / generated field shape / reference round-trip / unreachable-server fallback). No TEST-ID leans on another's assertion.

REJECTED — `expect(options).toHaveCount(MOCK_TOOL_NAMES.length)` is not an assertion over a possibly-empty collection: `openToolList` (:87-92) first waits for `[data-testid^="wf-builder-tool-name-opt-"]`.first() to be VISIBLE, so a listbox that renders nothing fails before the count is taken, and the sorted testid comparison at :173-179 then pins identity, not just cardinality.

REJECTED — TEST-18's absence assertion `not.toMatch(/prompt_file|prompt:/i)` over `body.innerText()` carries an explicit positive control on the very same captured string (`expect(bodyText).toContain(HUMAN.agentPromptMissing)`, :210), so a page that failed to render, or an empty innerText, cannot make it pass.

REJECTED — the per-finding clipping loop is NOT a loop over a possibly-empty collection: `expect(findingCount).toBeGreaterThan(0)` is asserted inside the viewport loop (:148-151), i.e. at every one of the three widths, and a pre-loop `expect(byTestId(page,'wf-builder-finding').first()).toBeVisible()` (:122-124) guards the setup. Same for the 390px column check, which asserts `boxes.length === SEARCH_PROPERTY_NAMES.length` (:198-200).

REJECTED — the two 403 tests were checked for the classic 'a 403 that proves nothing' shape. They do not have it: test 3 carries an explicit 200 positive control on a server the outsider DOES own (:278-284) before asserting 403 on the other user's server, and both tests discriminate the refusing layer by `error_code` (INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS vs USER_NO_ACCESS) rather than by status alone. Test 2 also registers a REAL server id so the 403 cannot be a 'no such row' artifact.

REJECTED — TEST-7's 'an arbitrary name COMMITS' leg is asserted only as the ABSENCE of 'A tool name is required' with no prior positive assertion that the message was ever present, which looked vacuous. It is not, because the same commit is independently proven downstream: `waitBuilderValid` (:379) requires the backend to stop emitting WORKFLOW_TOOL_NO_TOOL, and the post-reload `toHaveValue('an_unlisted_tool')` (:388-391) proves the value actually persisted.

REJECTED — TEST-2 was examined for the tautology shape (asserting the implementation rather than the design promise). It is not one: three steps, two broken for DIFFERENT codes, the THIRD and valid step selected, per-finding `data-step-id` counts (1 vs 2 vs 0), a repo-wide `toHaveCount(2)` on invalid markers, badge counts matching the per-step finding counts, and two goto clicks landing on two DIFFERENT step kinds. Every one of those goes red if attribution were hardcoded, derived from selection, or derived from 'the workflow is invalid'.
